chapter: Society work, Camilla Todd and Storyville
title: Moret's large concert orchestras at the Country Club
summary: Mr. Moret assembled 50 to 75 players for concerts; no jazz was played and Matoyi handled the cadenzas.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Orleans Country Club playing concert music. You did? As large as that? How many? 75 or 80?

Mr. Moret used to have sometimes 50 to 75 pieces playing at the background sometimes playing concert. Old Eugene Moret, I mean John Moret. I'm telling you that man used to have some orchestras of time. He used to pick up all the musicians that he could pick up in New Orleans, you know, and make a few
rehearsals, you see. And then we'd play those concerts. Did you try your jazz compositions too as a whole group? No, no. It was just a song. Just a song. That's right.

Because Mr. Moret couldn't play no jazz, you see. He never did play no jazz. And whenever he'd have those concerts like that, there wasn't no jazz at all. And this fellow I'm telling you about, Matoyi, he's the one who used to do all the cadence work. He did? Yes. And we had some trumpet player there, but Matoyi was always the one that was picked for the cadence. Oh. But he went down, huh? Oh yeah. But I don't want him to go down if they don't hold up.
